newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS Holding nine-month net profit unchanged.
newsitem.headline: CS Holding nine-month net profit unchanged.

text.p: Switzerland's CS Holding said on Monday group gross income rose 12 percent in the first nine months of 1996 despite a slowdown in the third quarter itself but net income was unchanged from the year-earlier period.
It said it expected a higher operating result for the full year 1996 but cautioned that provisions for credit risk would remain high due to a weak Swiss economy.

"Despite a slowing of the rate of growth in the third quarter, CS Holding's consolidated gross income after the first nine months of 1996 was 12 percent above last year's equivalent figure," it said in a statement.

"With provisions for endangered credit positions still high, as expected, and with costs recording a further slight rise, the net profit for the first three quarters of the year was on a par with last year's," it said.
CS Holding said its net result for the full year would depend on the level of provisions.

"We expect our operating result for 1996 to be higher than last year; however, business performance in the final quarter will depend to some extent on the state of the financial markets and the net result will depend upon provisions for credit risk which will remain at a high level," it said.

It said third-quarter gross earnings from the three main sources of income -- net income from balance-sheet business, net commission income and trading income -- were all between 3.5 percent and 6.5 percent below the first-half average, but in all rose 18 percent from the first nine months of 1995.
Staff expenses and other operating costs in the third quarter were in line with first-half developments. Overall costs were 18 percent higher than in the first nine months of 1995.
Credit-related provisions were, as expected, higher than for the same period last year, reflecting the Swiss economy's continued sluggishness.
